'''Ruth Ingrid Michler''' (March 8, 1967 to November 1, 2000)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Ruth Michler biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Michler/ |access-date=2024-05-27 |website=MacTutor Index}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Melles |first=Caroline Grant |date=2003 |title=Dedication |url=https://pi.math.cornell.edu/News/2006-2007/michler_dedication.html |journal=Topics in Algebraic and Noncommutative Geometry: Proceedings in Memory of Ruth Michler |series=Contemporary Mathematics |language=en |location=Providence, Rhode Island |publisher=American Mathematical Society |volume=324 |issue= |doi=10.1090/conm/324 |isbn=0821832093 |mr=2017395 |access-date=2025-08-07}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Iarrobino |first=A. |title=Commemorating Dr. Ruth Michler |url=https://web.northeastern.edu/iarrobino/~michler/Commem |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240219174557/https://web.northeastern.edu/iarrobino/~michler/Commem |archive-date=2024-02-19 |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=web.northeastern.edu}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=The Valuation Theory Home Page: Very Sad News |url=https://math.usask.ca/fvk/ruth.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190127152648/https://math.usask.ca/fvk/ruth.htm |archive-date=2019-01-27 |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=University of Saskatchewan Mathematics}}</ref> was an American-born mathematician of German descent who lived and worked in the United States. She earned her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in [[Mathematics]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]],<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Ruth Ingrid Michler |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=32774 |access-date=2025-08-06 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> and she was a tenured associate professor at the [[University of North Texas]]. She died at the age of 33 while visiting [[Northeastern University]], after which at least three memorial conferences were held in her honor, and the [[Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize]] was established in her memory.

== Early years ==
Michler was the daughter of German mathematician {{ill|Gerhard O. Michler|de}} and was born in [[Ithaca, New York]] while her family was visiting [[Cornell University]] from Germany.<ref name=":0" /> She grew up in Germany, living in [[Tübingen]], [[Giessen]], and [[Essen]].<ref name=":1" /> She completed her undergraduate studies in 1988 at the [[University of Oxford]], graduating summa cum laude.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |date=January–February 2001 |title=In Memoriam |url=https://www.drivehq.com/folder/p8755087/1748796012.aspx |journal=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]] Newsletter |volume=31 |issue=1 |access-date=2025-08-06}}</ref>

== Doctoral studies and research ==
Michler earned her Ph.D. in mathematics in 1993 from the University of California, Berkeley. Her dissertation is titled "Hodge components of cyclic homology of affine hypersurfaces."<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{cite thesis
 | last = Michler | first = Ruth Ingrid
 | mr = 2690218
 | title = Hodge-components of cyclic homology of singular affine hypersurfaces
 | id = {{ProQuest|304042308}}
 | publisher = University of California, Berkeley
 | year = 1993}}</ref> Her advisors were [[Mariusz Wodzicki]] and [[Arthur Ogus]]. She spent the 1993–1994 academic year as a postdoc at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] working with Leslie Roberts. In 1994, she joined the tenure-track faculty at the University of North Texas where she earned tenure in 2000.

== Memorial conferences and prize ==
Michler was killed in an accident in [[Boston]] on November 1, 2000, when she was struck by a construction vehicle while on her bicycle.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Iarrobino |first=Anthony |title=Tragic Accident |url=http://mathserver.neu.edu/~iarrobino/mathindex.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302171705/http://mathserver.neu.edu/~iarrobino/mathindex.html |archive-date=2021-03-02 |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=Northeastern University, Department of Mathematics}}</ref><ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2000-11-02 |title=Bicyclist killed at Northeastern |url=https://www.seacoastonline.com/story/news/2000/11/02/bicyclist-killed-at-northeastern/51306015007/ |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=Portsmouth Herald |language=en-US |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Several conferences were organized in her honor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Iarrobino |first=A. |title=Conferences Commemorating Dr. Ruth Michler |url=https://web.northeastern.edu/iarrobino/~michler/RMCommemConf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240219174557/https://web.northeastern.edu/iarrobino/~michler/RMCommemConf |archive-date=2024-02-19 |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=Northeastern University}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/meetings/awm-jmm/awm-at-jmm-2011/|title=AWM at JMM 2011|website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM)|language=en-US|access-date=2019-01-26}}</ref> Two conferences resulted in a volume of papers dedicated to her memory<ref>{{cite book
 | last1 = Melles | first1 = Caroline Grant
 | last2 = Brasselet | first2 = Jean-Paul
 | last3 = Kennedy | first3 = Gary
 | last4 = Lauter | first4 = Kristin
 | last5 = McEwan | first5 = Lee
 | doi = 10.1090/conm/324
 | isbn = 0-8218-3209-3
 | mr = 2017395
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | series = Contemporary Mathematics
 | title = Proceedings of the Conference "Resolution of Singularities and Noncommutative Geometry" held in Luminy, July 20–22, 2001 and the Algebraic Geometry Conference held in Annapolis, MD, October 25–28, 2001, Dedicated to the memory of Ruth Michler
 | volume = 324
 | year = 2003}}</ref> In 2007 the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] inaugurated the [[Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize]] which is "awarded annually to a woman recently promoted to Associate Professor or an equivalent position in the mathematical sciences".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/ruth-i-michler-prize/|title=Ruth I. Michler Prize|website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM)|language=en-US|access-date=2019-01-26}}</ref>
